# Evidence-based check: what does final *-a become in Phan Rang Cham?
# Data (proto, cham) from the problem for proto words ending in -a.
data = [("lima", "limɨ"), ("mata", "mɨta"), ("bara", "pirà"), ("bala", "pilà")]

def final_vowel_change(proto, cham):
    # compare the final vowel and the consonant preceding it
    return proto[-2], proto[-1], cham[-2], cham[-1]

nasal = set("mnŋ")
rule_ok = True
for p, c in data:
    pc, pv, cc, cv = final_vowel_change(p, c)
    print(f"*{p} -> {c}: preceding C={pc!r}, final proto V={pv!r}, cham final V={cv!r}")
    if pc in nasal:
        rule_ok &= (cv == "ɨ")
    else:
        # non-nasal: final -a is preserved (maybe with grave accent à)
        rule_ok &= (cv in ("a", "à"))
print("Rule 'final a -> ɨ only after nasal, else a/à' fits all data:", rule_ok)

# Consonant correspondences relevant to *dəpa
# *d -> t word-initially/medially (dikiʔ->takiʔ, dilah->talàh, padam->patàm)
# *ə -> a in first syllable (bəsey -> pathey)
# *p -> p (paley->paley, paday->patày)
# grave accent appears only when the 2nd-syllable onset is voiced (r,l,b,d,j); here p is voiceless
# (cf. batuk->patuʔ, basah->pathah, dikiʔ->takiʔ: no grave)
pred = "t" + "a" + "p" + "a"
claimed = "tapɨ"

# p is not nasal, so final -a should stay -a
if claimed == pred:
